clue.text: Forward with the Conservatives!

definitions.meaning: an attacking footballer playing wide on the right of the field
siding with the political right, as a Tory supporter does

explanation.surface: A rallying cry urging the country onward behind the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a football position on the right flank; the other is a person of right-leaning politics.

clue.text: Cuckoo pint-green, I'm sorry to say!

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of the hyphenated phrase are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone apologising for a strange green drink, a pint of the cuckoo-pint plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo pint' is a wild arum, but 'Cuckoo' is the anagram signal on PINTGREEN; 'I'm ... to say' is padding around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling contrition is being sorry for a wrong done.

clue.text: Circumspect in speaking about dud gear

indicators.note: about here means the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Being cagey when describing some faulty equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful or cautious speech is said to be guarded, as in a guarded reply.

clue.text: Captain of MCC's up in the air?

definitions.text: Captain of MCC's up in the air?

parts.words: Captain of MCC's up in the air?
parts.note: a captain in the cricketing sense leads a Test side, while an aircraft captain flies one; an airborne Test captain is the reading

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the cricket club's captain is undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, which once ran England's Test tours; 'up in the air' looks like 'undecided' but means literally flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flies new aircraft to trial them, a flier on trial, is pictured as a Test skipper aloft.

clue.text: Deduce one is mink-clad, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the word for the description is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: wearing mink means dressed in fur, two words run together

explanation.surface: Concluding that someone is wearing a mink coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a conclusion from evidence is to work it out logically.

clue.text: Weary Ted dressed in female attire

indicators.note: in places the shuffled name inside the garment word

parts.note: a gown is a woman's dress

indicators.note: dressed suggests the letters of the name are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ted, tired out, has put on women's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Ted in drag; 'Weary' is a verb here, to tire someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone down is to depress or tire them, making them weary.

clue.text: Wake-up Tours' in liquidation?

indicators.note: a company in liquidation is broken up, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A tour company going bust gives its customers a rude awakening.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone from sleep or inactivity is to stir them awake.

clue.text: Brownie film?

parts.note: a Brownie was a Kodak box camera, and an old brown-toned photographic print fits a film that is brownish

explanation.surface: A movie about the junior Girl Guides.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are junior Girl Guides, but here the word just means brown-ish; old photographs had a reddish-brown tint.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownish pigment from cuttlefish ink gives old photos their warm brown tone.

clue.text: Who gets half cut? Patriots do

indicators.note: cut is slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Asking who is getting drunk, with patriots as the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' reads as one phrase for tipsy, but 'half' is fodder and 'cut' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Displaying national colours or making a patriotic appearance is what loyal citizens do.

clue.text: It's silly to stir pity in a very generous person

parts.note: soft can mean foolish or simple-minded
to touch someone is to move them emotionally

explanation.surface: It is foolish to arouse compassion in someone open-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easily persuaded to give money or help is an easy mark for generosity.

clue.text: Made compact-having one's back to the wall

definitions.text: having one's back to the wall
definitions.meaning: in serious difficulty, under great strain

explanation.surface: Something compressed, and someone cornered.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means squashed firmly, and idiomatically means struggling under heavy pressure.

clue.text: Pound we laid out gets us admit, ted

indicators.note: laid out suggests the letters are spread and arranged in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: We spent a pound and that got us let in.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess to a fault is to acknowledge it openly.

clue.text: Bird in kangaroo's territory

indicators.note: in says the bird sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A bird found in the land of the kangaroo.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an Australian bird, but the answer lies within the letters of 'kangaroo's territory'.
explanation.definitionFit: A male chicken, a cock, is a farmyard bird.

clue.text: Bronzed sportsman?

parts.note: bronzed suggests a suntan, but here means awarded the bronze medal, given to the one finishing behind gold and silver

explanation.surface: A tanned athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor placed after first and second receives bronze.

clue.text: Addicted to tea in a large two-handled vessel?

parts.note: being devoted to something is loving it
a cup is a serving of tea, as in a cup of tea

explanation.surface: A tea addict drinking from an enormous mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large drinking vessel with two handles passed round at banquets is the ceremonial bowl so named.

clue.text: Intensely glowing flare

parts.note: very means to a high degree
light means bright, shining

explanation.surface: A fiercely blazing flare.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light, named after its inventor Edward Very, is a coloured flare fired from a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal flare fired from a pistol is named after its American inventor.

clue.text: Religious term Alice misused

indicators.note: misused suggests the letters are put to wrong use, scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Alice has used a word wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar or nun of a Catholic order founded on Mount Carmel is a religious person.

clue.text: Whisker chopper!

definitions.meaning: something that whisks, such as a kitchen tool for beating eggs
slang for a helicopter, whose rotor resembles a kitchen beater

explanation.surface: A tool for cutting off a beard.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen gadget whisks eggs, and the same name is slang for a helicopter.

clue.text: One no longer held responsible for creating search parties

definitions.text: One no longer held responsible for creating search parties

parts.words: One no longer held responsible for creating search parties
parts.note: reads as someone cleared of blame, but describes a fugitive who has broken out and sent searchers after them

explanation.surface: Someone cleared of blame for organising hunting expeditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer held responsible' suggests being let off liability; 'held' means imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner who has fled captivity is no longer detained and prompts a manhunt.

clue.text: It takes money to seal our lips

definitions.meaning: a small bag that holds cash
to press the lips tightly together

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet comes at a price.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a wallet-like bag for coins; the verb means to pucker the lips shut.

clue.text: C in C one up over musician

indicators.note: over means the short word is turned over and placed above the rest

parts.note: taken as written
the letter as printed
the letter as printed
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A commander-in-chief outranking a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: C in C looks like commander-in-chief; here it is two Cs and IN. 'over' turns UP to PU and puts it at the top of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer of Tosca and La Bohème was a musician.

clue.text: I cry 'all out'—how beautifully imaginative!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shouting rapturously at a beautiful creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressive, poetic writing is song-like in its imaginative beauty.

clue.text: Wealthy Oriental in German state

indicators.note: in puts the compass letter inside the word for wealthy

parts.note: rich means wealthy
E is short for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A rich Easterner living in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for an empire or realm names the German state, as in the Third Reich.

clue.text: Behold rage of French runner

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
ire means anger

explanation.surface: Look at the fury of a French athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' in crosswords often means a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in France flows, or runs, to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Shock cases of girls hanging by their necks

definitions.text: Shock cases of girls hanging by their necks

parts.words: Shock cases of girls hanging by their necks
parts.note: a shock is a mass of hair, so these are little holders for locks of hair worn on chains round girls' necks, not grim hangings

explanation.surface: Appalling stories of young women being hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock cases' reads as horrifying incidents; a shock is a thick tuft of hair, the keepsake kept in such a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hinged pendants holding a keepsake such as a curl of hair are worn on a neck chain.

clue.text: Looking for a good time? Any thing but!

definitions.text: Looking for a good time? Any thing but!

parts.words: Looking for a good time? Any thing but!
parts.note: reads as seeking fun, but means looking for a very short time only, the opposite of a good long look

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker is asked if they want fun and denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good time' suggests a night out; here it means a long while, and the activity is a brief look.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching a fleeting sight of something is looking only momentarily.

clue.text: Story about the city of Paris

definitions.text: Story about the city of Paris

parts.words: Story about the city of Paris
parts.note: Paris is not the French capital but the Trojan prince, and his city was Troy, also called Ilium

explanation.surface: A tale set in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris the Trojan prince carried off Helen, starting the war told in Homer's epic named after Ilium, another name for Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem tells the tale of the siege of Troy, Paris's home city.

clue.text: Ploughing teams thrive-its important to farmers

indicators.note: ploughing turns over the soil, so the letters are turned over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Teams of horses or oxen flourish while ploughing, crucial for farm work.
explanation.definitionFit: The season of gathering crops is the key period of the agricultural year.
